intro.title: Build dead letter queue handling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a dead letter queue (DLQ) handler in Node.js to manage failed messages from a message queue. You will learn how to implement error handling to detect processing failures and route those messages to a separate queue for later analysis. The core programming concept involves using asynchronous operations and conditional logic to control message flow. You will work with JavaScript constructs like async/await, try-catch blocks, and queue management libraries. By the end, you'll have a functional DLQ system that improves application reliability by isolating problematic messages.
intro.usecase: Dead letter queue handling is essential in production systems like e-commerce platforms where payment processing messages might fail due to expired cards or inventory issues. In logistics dashboards, failed shipment tracking updates are moved to DLQs for manual review and retry. Financial services use DLQs to isolate failed transaction alerts that need investigation before reprocessing. This pattern ensures critical business operations continue while problematic messages are quarantined for debugging.
